title: Adopt a clean-break Learn-it generation without RC718 data compatibility
purpose: Replace the previously planned compatibility resolver, identity overlay and learner-state migration path with a clean-break product generation. RC718 remains available as the frozen legacy standalone product, while the next generation starts with a new contract, new storage namespace, canonical identity from inception and no automatic reading or migration of RC718 libraries, progress, sessions, bilans, retention or local customizations.
invariants: RC718 and its promoted artifact remain immutable and available as the legacy standalone generation.
This work package changes no Player, stored data, import contract, release artifact or runtime behavior.
The accepted learnit-identity-v1 taxonomy remains the target identity model for the new generation.
The compatibility resolver, identity overlay, dual-read window and transactional migration of RC718 learner state are cancelled unless a future accountable-owner decision explicitly reopens them.
The new generation must use a distinct storage namespace and must never silently read, overwrite or reinterpret RC718 state.
RC718 kits are not accepted directly by the new generation; content must be regenerated or deliberately converted and validated under the new contract.
Backend, accounts, synchronization, remote catalog, commerce, tenancy and marketplace remain held.
No compatibility code may be introduced merely to reduce the visible cost of the chosen rupture.
concessionsAccepted: Existing local libraries are not transferred automatically.
Plan and course display-name customizations are not transferred automatically.
Progress, active sessions, bilans, points to review and retention history restart from zero.
Existing RC718 kits require regeneration or explicit conversion before use.
The new generation is a product break, not a transparent upgrade.
requiredSafeguards: Keep the RC718 source, tested artifact, manifests, hashes and human evidence immutable and retrievable.
Use storage keys and durable database names that cannot collide with RC718.
Fail closed on legacy payloads rather than interpreting them partially.
Provide an explicit human-facing release note before any new-generation human test or distribution.
Prove that opening the new generation cannot mutate RC718 localStorage or IndexedDB data.
Bind source, contract, build, tests, artifact and hashes atomically for the first new-generation candidate.

rollback.designRollback: Revert this work package and its four companion governance files before any new-generation implementation starts.
rollback.productFallback: Continue using the frozen RC718 artifact; no RC718 data has been changed by this decision.
rollback.postImplementation: Rollback means distributing RC718 again or reverting the bounded new-generation candidate. It does not mean migrating new-generation data back into RC718.

acceptance.humanDecision: Accountable owner explicitly selected trajectory C and stated that no current justification warrants continuity costs.

nextGate.purpose: Design and authorize the minimum viable clean-generation foundation: new major content contract, isolated storage namespace, canonical identity rules, regenerated golden kits, exact bounded file plan and release gates. No compatibility or migration layer is permitted.
